title: Semigroup-dressed Petz collar for smooth cutoff removal
status: PROPOSED BREAKTHROUGH ROUTE; NO PROOF GATE CLOSED
question: Can a heat-semigroup spectral collar replace the rank-changing hard energy projector in the recoverability-first route, giving a dimension-safe local Petz transport interface and an explicit Euclidean-to-real-time bridge?

motivation: R-394 and R-395 make the hard-window tail and trace disturbance explicit, but their adjacent-cutoff ratios remain large.
R-396 verifies projected Petz transport, while its transported-error profile still has a finite adjacent-cutoff ratio of 6.91143733666218.
A heat-semigroup filter is analytic in the local positive energy and has no rank jumps, so cutoff changes can be differentiated before taking a limit.
The same filter is a Euclidean-time collar, allowing reflection-positive semigroup composition to be kept separate from the later Lorentzian continuation.
new_perspective.qft_interface: Use the Euclidean collar parameter s as an OS/KMS-compatible smoothing coordinate; do not identify it with physical time until a common generator and analytic continuation have been proved.

mathematical_contract.shifted_energy: K_L=H_L-inf(sigma(H_L)) is positive on each finite local core.
mathematical_contract.filter: F_s=exp(-s K_L/2), s>0, with F_s F_t=F_(s+t).
mathematical_contract.filtered_state: rho_s=F_s rho F_s / m_s, where m_s=Tr(rho exp(-s K_L)).
mathematical_contract.mass_identity: 1-m_s=Tr(rho(1-exp(-s K_L))) <= s Tr(rho K_L), using 1-exp(-s x)<=s x for x>=0.
mathematical_contract.local_reference: For A-B-C, sigma_s is the filtered state and R_s is the Petz map built from (sigma_s)_BC and (sigma_s)_B.
mathematical_contract.open_gentle_function: The finite verifier must determine a sharp normalized-filter disturbance envelope Phi(s M1); no such envelope is assumed by this route.
mathematical_contract.derivative_target: For s,t>0, bound the local observable action of F_s-F_t by the exact scalar functional-calculus modulus, with constants independent of oscillator cutoff and volume on the selected common core.

finite_discriminator.fixture: Reuse every R-396 volume, orientation, core width, buffer width, beta and energy-window row, adding s in {1/8,1/4,1/2,1,2}.
primary_checks: Compute m_s, rho_s and the exact filtered Petz map without hard spectral rank selection.
Check positivity, trace normalization, semigroup composition and the scalar mass inequality on every row.
Measure projected and transported trace distances, the normalized-filter disturbance, and adjacent-s/dimension profiles.
Compare fixed-s and moment-scaled s choices; retain source, shape and beta profiles rather than only global maxima.
finite_discriminator.independent_checks: Rebuild the Hamiltonian, filter, reductions, square roots and Petz map without importing the primary module.
hostile_mutations: replace F_s by a hard projector while retaining the smooth bound
replace exp(-s K/2) by exp(-s K) in one leg only
drop either the ABC or AB displacement term from the transport budget

theorem_ladder.name: finite smooth-filter positivity and mass control
theorem_ladder.target: Prove the finite scalar functional-calculus identities and certify 0<m_s<=1 with the first-moment mass envelope.

theorem_ladder.name: dimension-free normalized-filter disturbance
theorem_ladder.target: Derive a trace or local observable disturbance bound that depends on s and a cutoff-independent local moment, not on log(dim).

theorem_ladder.name: smooth Petz transport
theorem_ladder.target: Compose SC-2 with R-396 recoverability and prove a local shell budget stable under adjacent cutoff changes.

theorem_ladder.name: Euclidean collar to common dynamics
theorem_ladder.target: Use semigroup composition and reflection positivity to identify a common local form core, then separately establish KMS and real-time generator continuation.

adversarial_review.check: A filtered state is normalized by m_s on every row and no lower bound on m_s is silently replaced by one.
The inequality 1-exp(-sK)<=sK is exact, but a cutoff-independent bound on Tr(rho K) is still a separate hypothesis.
The Petz map is built from the same filtered reference state on BC and B; replacing it by a rho-dependent map would invalidate transport comparison.
Semigroup positivity and OS reflection positivity do not by themselves imply a finite light cone, Lorentzian signature or physical-time generator.
A hard projector cannot be used to justify a smooth functional-calculus derivative; the hostile lane must distinguish the two.

promotion_criteria: All finite primary, independent, hostile and Lean checks pass with exact s and normalization sentinels.
A dimension-safe normalized-filter modulus is proved on a declared common local core, with its moment and beta hypotheses explicit.
The smooth transport profile has a cutoff-independent shell modulus on the declared source and shape grid before any Q3LOCK promotion.
The Euclidean collar is linked to, but not conflated with, the OS/KMS and real-time common-alpha obligations.
stop_conditions: If m_s approaches zero in the intended scaling or the disturbance grows with cutoff at every admissible s, retire this smooth-filter route and retain only the finite identities.
If every dimension-safe modulus requires a logarithmic dimension factor, do not relabel the finite Petz transport as uniform.
If semigroup composition produces a volume or history-length normalization loss, move back to the phase-conditioned folded-influence fallback.
If the Euclidean construction supplies no common core or real-time continuation, keep it as an OS-side finite collar only.
boundary: Claim-nonbearing route design. It proposes a smooth spectral and Euclidean collar but proves no new inequality, no common-alpha, no OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, no mass gap, no continuum, no C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The heat-semigroup filter is a candidate regularization and QFT interface; its finite mass identity is not a cutoff-uniform moment theorem and its positivity is not a Lorentzian causal cone.
